# `tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data`

**A `setQueryData` updater does not change the cached data in place**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-tanstack-query` (npm) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:tanstack-query/recommended` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the update has to be rewritten to build a new value) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |

## What it checks

The updater function passed to `setQueryData` or `setQueriesData` does not assign to, `delete` from,
increment, `Object.assign` onto or call an in-place array method (`push`, `splice`, `sort`, …) on its
argument, the data in the cache.

**Why:** The cache and every component reading it still hold the same object, so nothing re-renders and the
data a later update starts from is already changed. *Updates from Mutation Responses: "Updates via
`setQueryData` must be performed in an immutable way. **DO NOT** attempt to write directly to the
cache by mutating data (that you retrieved from the cache) in place."*

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-tanstack-query
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:tanstack-query/recommended` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:tanstack-query/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule tanstack-query/no-mutating-set-query-data  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                             # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Return a new value built from the old one: `{ ...old, title }`, `[...old, item]`,
   `old.filter(…)`, `old.map(…)`.
2. For deep updates, build the copy with Immer's `produce(old, (draft) => { … })`, which is
   where an in-place change is correct.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
queryClient.setQueryData(['posts', { id }], (oldData) => {
  if (oldData) {
    oldData.title = 'my new post title';
  }
  return oldData;
});
```

#### Do

```js
queryClient.setQueryData(['posts', { id }], (oldData) =>
  oldData ? { ...oldData, title: 'my new post title' } : oldData,
);
```

queryClient.setQueryData(['posts', { id }], (oldData) => {

## Differences from the source

The source is TanStack Query v5's Updates from Mutation Responses guide, not a lint rule. codelaw reads
an updater written in place and the changes made through its parameter's own name: a value taken out of
it first (`const page = old.pages[0]`), or an item a callback receives (`old.map((p) => { p.seen = true })`),
is not followed. An updater that reassigns its parameter (`old = { ...old }`) is not checked. The method
is recognised by its name, on any object.
